transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is that I don’t feel like myself lately. The stuff that usually kind of keeps me going—like my photography walks, and I help mentor some kids sometimes, and even just keeping my calendar clean, which I’m usually really particular about because in my job if the calendar’s a mess everything gets weird—those things all started feeling… flat. Heavy, I guess.

I keep meaning to do them, but then I just don’t start. Like I’ll think, “I should go take photos,” and then I’m still sitting there an hour later. So… that’s why I figured I should talk to someone.
Do you still enjoy the activities you mentioned, like photography and mentoring, when you do manage to start them?

Sort of… I mean, if I actually get out the door with the camera, there might be a moment where I notice the light on a building or something, and I think, “Oh, that’s nice.” But it doesn’t really carry me the way it used to.

It’s more like everything leading up to it feels heavy, and even the things that usually make me feel like me—photography, mentoring, keeping my calendar neat—they’ve just gotten kind of flat. Like I know I care about them, or I used to, but I don’t start them the same way. I’ll sit there meaning to do it, and then… I don’t.
Do you still feel pleasure when you're doing things that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… not really in the same way. I mean, I can recognize that something is nice, like if I’m out with my camera and the light hits right, but it doesn’t feel like it used to.

It’s like the things that usually make me feel like myself—photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean—started feeling kind of flat and heavy. And then I just… stopped starting them. Which is weird, because I’m usually the person who keeps all that moving, especially with calendars—my whole job kind of depends on that. But lately I’ll think about doing it and then just sit there.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad most of the day. It’s more like… blank? Or slowed down.

Like, I’ll sit at my desk and stare at the calendar, and usually I’m good at that—color-coding things, moving meetings around, all of it—and lately it’s just like the boxes are there but I’m not really in them, if that makes sense.

So… sad, maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure that’s the main word I’d use.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight lately?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been checking, honestly. My scale is kind of tucked behind this stack of boxes in the bathroom closet—well, not boxes exactly, more like those plastic bins I keep meaning to label—so I don’t really look.

My clothes don’t feel wildly different, I guess. Nothing I’ve noticed enough to think, “Oh, I lost weight,” or “I gained weight.” So… I don’t know, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah, sleep’s been… kind of off. Some nights I’ll only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I’m awake before it’s even light out.

And the weird thing is I don’t always feel tired right away. I’ll be lying there thinking, well, I could just answer a few emails, or fix the appointment lists, because if I don’t do it then the whole thing gets messy—though honestly, nobody’s asking me to do it at 4 in the morning. I just feel ready to start, like my brain clicked on too early.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual?

Maybe, yeah… not like I’m walking in slow motion exactly, but everything feels heavier to start.

Like the stuff that usually kind of makes me feel like me—going out with my camera, taking one of those long photography walks, checking in with the kids I mentor, even keeping my calendar neat—those things started feeling flat. I’d think, “I should do that,” and then I just… wouldn’t initiate it.

And I know that’s not the same as moving slowly, but it feels like I’m pushing through wet cement or something. Even opening the calendar, which is usually my whole thing, feels like this big chore.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy and look forward to?

I mean… I want to say yes, because usually I’d look forward to taking my camera out, you know, like just walking around and noticing light on buildings or weird little details. Or mentoring the kids—usually that gives me something to feel good about.

But lately those things just feel kind of flat. Heavy, maybe. Like even keeping my calendar clean, which sounds boring but is usually satisfying to me—I’ll color-code it and fix the spacing, that kind of thing—now I just look at it and don’t start. That’s kind of what made me come in, honestly. I stopped initiating the things that usually make me feel like myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… longer than I want to admit. About a year and three months, I think.

It kind of started after my family member’s health and behavior changed, and I ended up taking on a lot more of the coordinating—appointments, calls, keeping track of things. At first I thought I was just being responsible, like, “Okay, I’m good at organizing, I can handle this.” But then it just sort of kept going, and somewhere in there I noticed I wasn’t feeling like myself anymore.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or that you're looking forward to doing?

Not really, no. I mean, I keep thinking I should be looking forward to the usual things—taking my camera out, going on one of those walks where I notice little signs or shadows, or checking in with the kids I mentor. Even my calendar, which sounds silly, but keeping it clean used to feel good.

But lately it’s like… I can see the activity sitting there, and I know it’s mine, but it feels flat and heavy. I don’t start. That’s kind of what finally made me come in.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I’d call it “lost” completely, because part of me still recognizes those things as mine, you know? Like photography walks—I used to notice reflections in windows, little crooked signs, stuff like that. And mentoring the kids usually meant something to me.

Even my calendar, honestly, which sounds ridiculous, but keeping it neat used to feel satisfying. Lately it all just feels flat and heavy, and I don’t really initiate any of it. That’s pretty much what made me come in.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?

I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly. That word feels… big, like a door closing. I’m not sure I’m there.

I guess I just don’t have a clear picture of the future right now. It’s more like when I look ahead, it’s blurry, and then I start thinking about all the little things I need to do—emails, schedules, whether I forgot to return someone’s call—and I get kind of pulled off track. So… not hopeless, maybe. Just hard to feel much about it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past year?

I don’t think so? I mean, I don’t really track it closely. My clothes seem mostly the same, I guess.

I did think about weighing myself when I was reorganizing the bathroom cabinet, because the scale was under this stack of old towels, and then I ended up sorting the towels instead, so… I’m not sure. But I haven’t noticed a big weight loss over the year, no.
Have you noticed any significant change in your clothing size over the past year?

Not that I’ve noticed, no. My clothes still seem to fit about the same.

I mean, I did have one pair of work pants that felt tighter, but I think that was after I washed them on the wrong setting, because the dryer in my building runs too hot sometimes. I’ve been meaning to put a note on it, actually, because people keep leaving lint in the trap and it’s—sorry. No, I don’t think my clothing size has changed significantly over the past year.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past year?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t calculated anything like 5%.

I don’t think I’ve lost that much, because my clothes seem about the same, like I said. But I also don’t weigh myself regularly, so I can’t give you a precise answer. The scale is there, I just—well, I usually notice the dust around it more than the number, and then I end up cleaning instead. So… I haven’t noticed a major weight loss, no.
Have you experienced any noticeable weight loss over the past year?

Not really, no—not anything I’ve noticed. I mean, I don’t keep a careful record or anything, and the scale kind of just sits there in the bathroom. I moved it once because it was in the way of the cabinet door, and then I started cleaning under the sink, so I didn’t actually weigh myself.

But as far as I can tell, my clothes fit about the same, and nobody’s said anything to me about looking thinner. So I wouldn’t say I’ve had noticeable weight loss over the past year.
Have you had any periods in the past year where you lost a lot of weight in a short amount of time?

No, I don’t think so. I can’t think of any stretch where I suddenly dropped a lot of weight.

There were maybe weeks where I was busier and didn’t pay much attention, like at work when the calendar gets jammed and people keep moving meetings around—then I forget to check things like that. But nothing where I noticed my clothes getting loose or people commenting or anything. So… not that I’m aware of.
How long have you been feeling this blank or slowed down sensation?

It’s been… about a year and three months, I think. Around then is when it started feeling like that.

It was after one of my family members had a change in their health and behavior, and I ended up taking on more of the coordinating—appointments, calls, keeping track of things. I’m used to organizing things at work, calendars and all that, but when it’s family it sort of follows you home, you know? Anyway, that’s about when I started noticing this blank or slowed-down feeling.
Do you feel that this blank or slowed-down sensation has been consistently present for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think it has been there most days, most of the day. Not every single minute, maybe, but enough that it’s hard to ignore.

What made me come in is that the things that usually make me feel like myself—like going out on photography walks, or mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar clean and organized—started feeling flat. Heavy, I guess. And then I’d just stop starting them. I’d think, “I should go do that,” and then I’d end up sorting a drawer or staring at the calendar colors instead, which… doesn’t really answer your question, sorry.

But yes, it’s been pretty consistently there.
Has this blank or slowed-down sensation been present for at least two years?

No, not two years. It’s more like… about a year and three months.

I remember it because it started after my family member’s health and behavior changed, and I started doing more of the coordinating—appointments, phone calls, keeping track of things. I already do that kind of thing at work, so at first I thought I was just tired from all the scheduling and organizing, but… that’s around when the blank, slowed-down feeling started.

doctor.question: Has this blank or slowed-down sensation been present for at least two years?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and three months, starting after my family member’s health and behavior changed and I took on more coordination.

patient.answer:
No, not two years. It’s more like… about a year and three months.

I remember it because it started after my family member’s health and behavior changed, and I started doing more of the coordinating—appointments, phone calls, keeping track of things. I already do that kind of thing at work, so at first I thought I was just tired from all the scheduling and organizing, but… that’s around when the blank, slowed-down feeling started.
